title: Can I Win
summary: Given the maximum integer maxChoosableInteger and a target sum desiredTotal, determine if the first player can force a win by optimally selecting integers from 1 to maxChoosableInteger without repeating any integer.
statement: Given the maximum integer maxChoosableInteger and a target sum desiredTotal, determine if the first player can force a win by optimally selecting integers from 1 to maxChoosableInteger without repeating any integer. Both players play optimally.
constraints: Two optimal players alternate choosing an unused integer from 1 through the maximum. Choices are shared and cannot be reused.
The player reaching or exceeding the target wins. Target zero is already a first-player win; an unreachable target returns False.
hints: Winning means there exists a move that wins immediately or leaves the opponent unable to force a win.
The set of already-used numbers completely identifies the remaining choices and running total.
Memoize win(used_mask,needed). For each unused value, succeed if it reaches needed or the next state is losing.
Reject targets larger than the total sum before searching. The recursion depth is at most 20 because every move consumes a number.
editorial: Minimax examines every legal response, not just a greedy line of play. A used-number mask determines both the available pool and remaining target, so there are at most 2^m states. Each tries at most m moves. An unreachable total is not a win merely because the other player has no move. If the target equals the sum of all numbers, exactly m turns are required and parity determines the winner. The oracle fills a separate retrograde table bottom-up.

tests.explanation: Whatever the first pick x, the second player can choose 11-x and reach 11. The first player cannot force a win.
Pick 1 first. Any opponent pick leaves an unused number that lets the first player reach 6 on the next turn.
